name: Autodrome de Linas-Montlhéry Piste de Vitesse (Speed Oval) Anneau
notes: The Piste de Vitesse, Montlhéry's banked concrete speed bowl, built in 1924 by the industrialist Alexandre Lamblin to plans by the architect Raymond Jamin and inaugurated on 4 October 1924. Two steeply banked parabolic turns joined by a pair of short straights make up 2,548 m of concrete on which cars could hold well over 200 km/h, and the bowl became Europe's premier venue for distance and endurance records. This layout runs the anneau on its own in the anti-clockwise direction used for record attempts; Grand Prix races took the banking the other way.
author: Legion
